findings.evidence: Model.lean:100 `def modelPdf (Flavor) (a b) := fun _ x _ => Set.indicator (Set.Icc 0 1) (betaShape a b) x`; Basic.lean:245 `def weight w f := fun i x Q2 => w i * f i x Q2`; Model.lean:166 `assumptions_modelPdf`; Model.lean:230 `sumRuleAssumptionsWeightModelPdfZeroOne (hw : ∑ i, w i = 6) : SumRuleAssumptions (weight w (modelPdf Flavor 0 1))` with `valenceTarget i := w i / 2`; Model.lean:221 `sum_mellinMoment_one_weight_modelPdf_zero_one`.
findings.fix: Define `threeQuarkPdf := PDF.weight w (PDF.modelPdf (Species Unit) 0 1)` (or drop the definition and use that term) and derive the integrability and valence-number lemmas from `assumptions_modelPdf`, `Assumptions.weight` and `sumRuleAssumptionsWeightModelPdfZeroOne hw` instead of re-proving them. Keep `sum_mellinMoment_one_threeQuarkPdf` as is, since its point is that it follows from the double-parton sum rules.
findings.issue: `threeQuarkPdf` is a new public definition of a density the library already has: `PDF.weight w (PDF.modelPdf (Species Unit) 0 1)` with `w s = if s = .quark () then 6 else 0` is pointwise `indicator (Icc 0 1) (fun x => 6*(1-x))` on the quark and `0` elsewhere. Its API duplicates existing lemmas: `integrableOn_threeQuarkPdf` (line 383) re-proves `assumptions_modelPdf` + `Assumptions.weight`, and `valenceNumber_threeQuarkPdf` (line 393) re-proves what `sumRuleAssumptionsWeightModelPdfZeroOne` already gives (`valenceTarget i = w i / 2`, so `3 - 0 = 3`).

findings.evidence: grep of the new file shows no occurrence of `Assumptions`, `IsPartonDensity`, `Regularity` or `SumRuleAssumptions` outside the new `NumberSumRule`/`MomentumSumRule` names; the comparable model in PDF/Model.lean exports `isPartonDensity_modelPdf`, `regularity_modelPdf`, `assumptions_modelPdf`, `sumRuleAssumptionsWeightModelPdfZeroOne`.
findings.fix: Expose `isPartonDensity_threeQuarkPdf`/`assumptions_threeQuarkPdf` and a `SumRuleAssumptions threeQuarkPdf` bundle (valence targets 3, 0, 0; momentum from `sum_mellinMoment_one_threeQuarkPdf`). The fix in the previous finding supplies all of these by inheritance.
findings.issue: The exposed model carries none of the bundles that characterize a `Pdf` in this repo: no `IsPartonDensity threeQuarkPdf`, no `Regularity`/`Assumptions`, no `SumRuleAssumptions`. A consumer therefore cannot feed the model to any existing theorem that takes `Assumptions f` (e.g. `mellinMoment_integrable`, `momentum_sumRule`, `valence_sumRule`), even though all four fields are immediate for it.

findings.evidence: OrderedSimplexIntegral.lean:244 `@[simp, measurability] lemma measurableSet_orderedRegion`; OrderedSimplexIntegral.lean:413 the same for `measurableSet_descendingRegion`; UnitTriangle.lean:55 has a bare `theorem`.
findings.issue: `measurableSet_unitTriangle` carries no automation attribute, so downstream `measurability` calls and side conditions of set-integral lemmas over `unitTriangle` cannot be discharged automatically; the directly analogous region lemma in this repo carries `@[simp, measurability]`.

summary: The double-parton surface (NumberSumRule/MomentumSumRule, their Iff.rfl restatements, the consistency theorems and the triangle Fubini API) is well-formed, but the exposed single-parton model duplicates PDF.weight/PDF.modelPdf and re-proves its API while carrying none of the Pdf-interface bundles, and the triangle's measurability lemma lacks the automation attribute its in-repo analogue carries.
